newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee adjusted down against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee adjusted down against the dollar.

text.p: The State (central) Bank of Pakistan said on Wednesday it has adjusted the rupee down to 40.2400/40.4412 to the dollar from 40.1200/40.3206 fixed on October 22.

The central bank gave no reason for the lower adjustment in the rupee value but bankers said the move was expected as the dollar had appreciated quite sharply in the past six months against other major currencies in the international markets.

They said with inflation running close to 12 percent, a stuborn trade deficit and strong dollar in the international markets the central bank had to reassess the value of the rupee to make Pakistani exports competitive.
The rupee has depreciated by 14.43 percent since the beginning of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June), compared to a depreciation of 13.24 percent in the year-ago period.
